meta_description: Agents earn autonomy in tiers: what they may do alone, with approval, never.

blocks.x: Agents earn autonomy in tiers: what they may do alone, with approval, never.
The policy envelope is the product — the argument in one line. Autonomy granted without policy is liability; policy without telemetry is fiction.
Replay evaluation on historical cases catches the 20% variance that breaks scripts.
Escalation design is where agent programs win or lose operator trust.

Where the policy envelope is the product breaks in practice: autonomy granted faster than governance — agents shipped with policies nobody wrote down and telemetry nobody reads, until the incident review becomes the real policy meeting.

Against the policy envelope is the product, the strongest counter-case is worth naming: the policy-first thesis can ossify into approvals that cost more than the work. Autonomy tiers need revisiting on a cadence, not once at launch.
How we put it to work

In delivery, the policy envelope is the product becomes a specific discipline: the build is a governed agent fleet: policies that bound what each agent may do, telemetry that shows what it did, and replay for when anyone asks why. Every program in the Agentic AI & Hyperautomation domain carries the same obligations — a signed baseline, named gate criteria, and evidence generated by running the system rather than preparing for a meeting.
If the policy envelope is the product is on your agenda this year, a briefing will tell you in 45 minutes whether this pattern fits your estate.
